items.capacity: Chief Global Affairs Officer (first holder of the role)
items.fact: Anthropic announced on 4 Aug 2026 that Cuéllar will join as its first Chief Global Affairs Officer, leading policy, international engagement and government relationships. The Anthropic page gives no effective start date; Wikipedia (read) describes him as Chief Global Affairs Officer at Anthropic.
items.quote: will join Anthropic as its first Chief Global Affairs Officer
items.missing: Effective start date. Anthropic gives only the announcement date.
items.notes: Search snippet (not read): socialsciencespace says his CASBS and Knight-Hennessy posts end 10 Aug 2026. Harvard Crimson 4 Aug 2026 (snippet, not read) calls him a Harvard Corporation member.

items.fact: Anthropic announced on 21 Jan 2026 that Cuéllar had been appointed a Trustee of the Long-Term Benefit Trust. Anthropic's 4 Aug 2026 announcement says he has since stepped down from the Trust to join the company.
items.quote: announced the appointment of Mariano-Florentino (Tino) Cuéllar as a new member of the Trust
items.missing: Date he left the Trust. The 4 Aug page says only that he stepped down to join the company.
items.notes: A TechJack Solutions snippet (not read) lists him as a current trustee; Anthropic's own page is preferred. Anthropic's Jul 2026 listing for a Bernanke appointment is a related item only.

items.fact: Carnegie announced on 15 Jan 2026 that Cuéllar would step down as president in July 2026 after nearly five years. Wikipedia (read) gives the term as 31 Oct 2021 to 1 Jul 2026. Anthropic's 4 Aug 2026 page says he 'recently stepped down' as president.
items.quote: will step down in July 2026 after nearly five years leading the institution
items.missing: The 2021 start date comes from Wikipedia, not from the Carnegie release. Whether he holds any Carnegie title after July 2026.
items.notes: Carnegie release said Avril Haines would succeed him as eleventh president (per a search snippet of the same page).

items.fact: Wikipedia's infobox (read) gives his California Supreme Court term as 5 Jan 2015 to 30 Oct 2021. Anthropic's Aug 2026 page confirms he was a Justice of the Supreme Court of California but gives no dates.
items.missing: Primary record of the appointment and term dates (court or governor's office).
items.notes: Anthropic 4 Aug page also describes him as director of Stanford's Freeman Spogli Institute and a Senior Fellow at Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered AI. Wikipedia also lists him as Cameron Schrier Family Professor of Law at Stanford.

items.from: Jack Clark; Sarah Heck; Tarun Chhabra; Michael Sellitto
items.capacity: Clark: co-founder, leads The Anthropic Institute, to assume Head of Public Benefit. Heck: Head of Public Policy. Chhabra: head of national security policy. Sellitto: title unresolved (see fact).
items.fact: Anthropic's page (11 Mar 2026, read) says co-founder Jack Clark leads The Anthropic Institute and 'will assume a new role as Anthropic's Head of Public Benefit'. The same page says Sarah Heck, who joined as Head of External Affairs, will lead Public Policy; before Anthropic she was Head of Entrepreneurship at Stripe and led global entrepreneurship and public diplomacy policy at the White House National Security Council. The Aspen Security Forum profile (read) gives Tarun Chhabra as Head of National Security at Anthropic; earlier he was deputy assistant to the president and coordinator for technology and national security on the NSC, and from 2021 to 2025 coordinated US technology competition with China. Michael Sellitto: a LongTermWiki table lists 'Head of Global Affairs, 2022 to present' but is marked 'Failed source check'; another profile lists 'Head of Geopolitics and Security' (search snippet only; the scai.gov.sg profile returned 404 when read). His earlier roles (Stanford HAI deputy director; NSC cybersecurity director 2015 to 2018) come from a search snippet only.
items.quote: will lead this team as Head of Public Policy
items.missing: Jack Clark's earlier public roles: not found in any read source. Sellitto's current title is unconfirmed. Start dates for Heck, Chhabra and Sellitto at Anthropic are not stated in read sources.
items.notes: Chhabra: Aspen profile https://www.aspensecurityforum.org/chhabra-tarun-2/ (read, says Anthropic head of national security policy). A USCC bio dated Feb 2026 (search snippet; PDF not read) lists him at Brookings and Hoover instead; the affiliation conflict is unresolved. Clark: LongTermWiki lists 'Co-founder, Head of Policy' from Jan 2021, marked 'Failed source check'.

items.to: Governments of Australia, Rwanda and Singapore (MOUs); UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (GOV.UK pilot)
items.capacity: MOU signatory (Australia, Rwanda, Singapore). Selected to build and pilot an assistant (UK DSIT, not described as an MOU).
items.fact: Rwanda: three-year MOU for health, education and public-sector AI, announced 17 Feb 2026 (Anthropic page, read); it codifies a fall 2025 education agreement. Australia: MOU on AI safety research, announced 31 Mar 2026 (Anthropic page, read); it commits to work with Australia's AI Safety Institute and to share Economic Index data. UK: on 27 Jan 2026 Anthropic said DSIT selected it 'to help build and pilot' an AI assistant for GOV.UK (Anthropic page, read). Singapore: unite.ai (read) reports an Anthropic announcement dated 14 Oct 2026 of a Singapore office and an MOU with the Ministry of Digital Development and Information; Anthropic's own announcement was not found. No Iceland, Japan or India agreement was found. The Anthropic Australia page says the MOU 'mirrors the arrangements we have with safety institutes in the US, UK, and Japan'; these are undated and not separately verified.
items.quote: Anthropic signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Australian government
items.missing: Primary texts of the MOUs (none read). Anthropic's own Singapore announcement. Any 2025 agreement with a non-US government beyond the Rwanda education deal and the UK DSIT work. Scope and dates of any UK MOU.
items.notes: Read pages: https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-rwanda-mou ; https://www.anthropic.com/news/gov-UK-partnership (27 Jan 2026; no dollar figure in matched excerpts) ; https://unite.ai/anthropic-signs-singapore-government-mou-as-new-office-opens (single outlet). Search snippets, not read: a Feb 2025 UK accord, ALX education partnership (Nov 2025).

items.capacity: Managing Director, International Affairs (title as reported)
items.fact: Reported 2 Sep 2026: Clifford will lead Anthropic's government relations outside the US across the UK, Europe, India and Asia-Pacific, based in London. Clifford's own words and Anthropic's own announcement about his remit were not found. The Guardian's report (read via freevacy syndication) is the source for the remit; DCD (read) gives the same title. Clifford stepped down as ARIA chair on 7 Sep 2026, five days after joining Anthropic (TNW, read); an earlier 2 Sep Guardian report had said he would stay on as chair.
items.quote: will lead the company's government relations outside the US
items.missing: Anthropic's own announcement; any statement by Clifford about his remit; the exact start date; confirmation of the title and reporting line.
items.notes: Resultsense 2 Sep 2026 (read): 'The investor who wrote Britain's AI action plan will lead Anthropic's dealings with governments outside America.' DCD 2 Sep 2026 (read): 'managing director of international affairs'. TNW 7 Sep 2026 (read): ARIA step-down; 'a government department had already reviewed that overlap'. A search snippet (newsbytes, read returned 403) says he reports to Cuéllar in a team of about 70; not verified.

items.capacity: Co-host with Rory Stewart (Clifford); guest (Cuéllar); The Rest Is Politics episode 'China Vs USA: Who Will Win the AI Race?'
items.fact: Podpulse (read) lists The Rest Is Politics episode 'China Vs USA: Who Will Win the AI Race?' dated 8 Jan 2026. It says Rory Stewart and Matt Clifford invited Tino Cuellar, then president of the Carnegie Endowment, to discuss the AI race. This is a documented joint public appearance before September 2026.

items.quote: inviting Tino Cuellar, president of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
items.missing: The show's own feed or site to confirm guest list and date. The podcast page was read only via an aggregator.
items.notes: Metacast and audioscrape listings returned 403 on read. A search snippet ties Stewart and Clifford to episode 493 with Cuéllar, which is unverified and may be a different episode.

items.to: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace; Anthropic leadership
items.fact: No documented contact between Clifford and the Carnegie Endowment, or between Clifford and Anthropic leadership, was found before September 2026. Carnegie 2026 events listing Cuéllar (21 Jan, 5 Feb and 20 May 2026; search snippets, not read) show no Clifford participation in the snippets. Cuéllar joined Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust on 21 Jan 2026 (T10.1b), a documented Cuéllar-Anthropic link that does not involve Clifford.
items.missing: Full Carnegie events archive for 2025 to 2026, and any Clifford event listing. Anthropic leadership calendar records (not public).
items.notes: Searches: 'Carnegie Endowment Matt Clifford Cuellar event 2026' (no Clifford result). Carnegie events pages cited from search snippets only.

items.capacity: London office lease, 158,000 sq ft, space for 800 staff
items.fact: Reported 16-17 Apr 2026: Anthropic took a 158,000 sq ft London lease at Regent's Place with space for about 800 staff, up from over 200 London staff (Shopifreaks, 16 Apr, read; Resultsense citing Wired, 17 Apr, read). Anthropic's Nov 2025 page (read) already names offices in London, Dublin and Zurich and says it tripled EMEA headcount in the past year.
items.quote: Anthropic signs a 158,000-sq-ft London lease with space for 800 staff
items.missing: Anthropic's own announcement of the lease; the lease start date; confirmed current London headcount (Resultsense calls 800 roughly four times the current UK headcount; Shopifreaks says 'over 200').
items.notes: Anthropic Nov 2025 page https://www.anthropic.com/news/new-offices-in-paris-and-munich-expand-european-presence (read): 'alongside our offices in London, Dublin, and Zurich'. Search snippet: first London office 2023, not read.
